thread:
alex_support: FYI customer Kestrel (dedicated) is reporting sustained 429s and tail latency spikes after a promotional push. They're seeing TPS SLO violations.

santiago_eng: Can you paste the admission/fallback logs? are burst credits showing as exhausted?

alex_support: Pasted key logs below, and yes burst credits appear low. 429s started ~08:42 UTC. Reports: tokens-per-second cap hit, admission control started rejecting.

alex_support: ```
admission-controller: admit=false reason=burst_credits_exhausted account=kestrel-team remaining=0
proxy: upstream_latency_ms=512 model=llama-13b-fp16 fallback=redwood-7b
runtime: kv_cache_miss=high seq_len=512 batch_size=1
```

maddy_ops: @santiago_eng can you check autoscaler events? maybe the dedicated pool didn't prewarm. also what's their autoscale policy (tps vs GPU util)?

santiago_eng: Running quick checks: `redwoodctl dedicated describe kestrel --since 30m` shows scale events were few. autoscale policy is cpu+gpu_util threshold, not tps. worth switching to tps-based headroom for bursty traffic.

carla_sre: Noting noisy-neighbor suspicion: same pool had a heavy finetune checkpoint job earlier today (cluster: pool-4). I see GPU memory pressure spikes around 08:30-08:55. That can tank admission headroom quickly.

ops-sre: Also seeing model routing fallbacks — some requests routed to the 7b variant which increases concurrency and KV cache churn. That can bump per-token compute and reduce effective tps.

alex_support: Customer also reported API auth 401s intermittently during the event. Could be token refresh storms from client retry logic. Any correlation with auth bursts?

billing-bot: Account kestrel-team burst_credit_bucket: capacity=100000 tokens current=0 last_refill=2026-01-10T00:00:00Z refill_rate=3600 tokens/hour

devops-bot: Noted: admission-controller pod restarted at 08:47 (OOM). `kubectl get pods -n redwood | grep admission-controller` shows 1/1 running now. Logs around restart: `panic: map insertion` then GC.

maddy_ops: Immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily increase headroom by bumping reserved capacity for kestrel-team (add 2 GPUs) 2) Throttle client retries via per-account rate limit 3) Add short-term burst refill (manual credit top-up) 4) Change autoscale policy to TPS-aware to pre-provision on traffic surges.

santiago_eng: Repro steps to validate fixes in staging: 1) run `redwood-loadgen --account=kestrel-team --tps=3500 --duration=10m --seq=512` 2) watch `redwoodctl metrics tail admission rejected_count,kvcache_miss,proxy_latency` 3) confirm no OOMs on admission controller and burst_credit remains >50000.

carla_sre: Root cause hypothesis: combination of exhausted burst credits + admission-controller OOM (restart window) + noisy neighbor GPU memory pressure = sudden loss of headroom and increased fallbacks to heavier model variant.

alex_support: Customer asked for timeline and cost impact. @billing-bot can we compute incremental cost if we top-up 200k tokens and add 2 GPU-hours during incident window?

billing-bot: Quick estimate: 200k token top-up = $12. reserved 2 x A10G for 2 hours (on dedicated) = ~$40. total ~ $52 (ballpark). Will open an invoice note for the credit.

ops-sre: Action items assigned: 
- santiago_eng: update autoscale policy template to include TPS-based headroom and run canary on pool-4 (ETA 3h)
- carla_sre: investigate admission-controller memory leak and add OOM alert (ETA 4h)
- maddy_ops: perform temporary capacity bump + manual burst refill and notify customer (now)
- alex_support: collect customer logs and confirm retry behavior (now)

alex_support: I'll open a support ticket with the timeline and proposed remediation, include this thread and the loadgen repro. Will ping customer once capacity bump is applied. :thumbsup:

santiago_eng: Also recommending long term: enforce soft isolation for heavy jobs (checkpointing/finetune) off the low-latency pools, improve model-routing cost heuristics to avoid fallback to heavier variants when admission headroom is low.

carla_sre: Adding note: consider KV cache hot-sharding for dedicated pools with high seq_len workloads to reduce cache misses under high concurrency.

alex_support: thanks all — I'll update thread after customer ack.

maddy_ops: marking incident as "support->dedicated-burst" and creating jira: RD-INC-2987.

ops-sre: closing loop: once we validate staging repro with `redwood-loadgen` we'll run a controlled promotion of the TPS autoscale policy to production for pool-4.

alex_support: Customer just confirmed bump applied and 429s dropped to near-zero. They want postmortem and a long-term plan.

santiago_eng: Good. I'll draft a short postmortem and remediation plan with timeline.
